Lemma
[Hopf boundary point lemma] Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0046 1. ch3:3.4\group ch03-classical-maximum-principle Suppose $L$ is uniformly elliptic, $c=0$, and $Lu\geq 0$ in $\Omega $. Assume that $u$ is continuous at $x_0\in \partial \Omega $, that $u(x_0)>u(x)$ for $x\in \Omega $, and that $\Omega $ has an interior sphere at $x_0$. If the outer normal derivative exists, then egin{equation} ag {3.10} rac{\partial u}{\partial u }(x_0)>0. \end{equation} If $c\leq 0$ and $c/\lambda $ is bounded, the same holds when $u(x_0)\geq 0$; when $u(x_0)=0$, no sign condition on $c$ is needed. More generally, within each fixed non-tangential cone at $x_0$, egin{equation} ag {3.11} \liminf _{x o x_0} rac{u(x_0)-u(x)}{|x-x_0|}>0. \end{equation}
Proof

\sketch If $B_R(y)\subset \Omega $ touches $x_0$, use on $B_R(y)\setminus \overline{B_ ho (y)}$ the barrier $v=e^{-\alpha |x-y|^2}-e^{-\alpha R^2}$. Uniform ellipticity and the coefficient bounds make $Lv\geq 0$ for large $\alpha $. The weak maximum principle applied to $u-u(x_0)+\varepsilon v$ gives $\partial _ u u(x_0)\geq -\varepsilon \partial _ u v(x_0)>0$ and also the non-tangential estimate. If $u(x_0)=0$, replace $L$ by $L-c^+$.

□
